202.1. Accessory. A use or structure customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or structure, and located on the same zoning lot as such a principal use or structure.
202.1.5. Accessory Dwelling Unit. An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is an accessory building occupied as a residence. Accessory buildings may be occupied as an ADU by another party so long as the primary dwelling unit on the property is owner-occupied. The ADU may be occupied by the property owner or rented. The unit must be aesthetically similar to the primary structure. The primary use of the lot must remain single-family, and the lot may not be subdivided nor may the accessory unit be sold separately.
202.2. Agriculture. The raising of soil crops or livestock in a customary manner on tracts of land at least three acres in size and shall include all associated activities. Retail selling of products raised on the premises shall be considered a permissible activity provided that space necessary for the parking of customers' vehicles shall be provided off the public right-of-way.
202.3. Alley. A secondary way which affords access to the side or rear of abutting property.
202.4. Alteration. Any change in the supporting members of a building; any addition to or reduction of a building; any change in use; or any relocation of a building.
202.4.5. Artist live/work studios. A single dwelling unit, either a One Family Attached Dwelling or a One Family Detached Dwelling, that is occupied by an artist to both live and work, where a minimum of thirty percent (30%) of the gross floor area of the unit is used for an artist studio by the artist residing therein.
202.5. Automobile Service Station. A land use where gasoline, oils, greases, batteries, tires, and general automobile accessories may be provided, but where no part of the premises is used for the storage or dismantling of wrecked or junked vehicles.
202.6. Block. A piece or parcel of land entirely surrounded by public highways or streets, other than alleys.
202.7. Boarding or Rooming House. A building used or intended for use as a place for lodging or feeding, or both, of three or more nonrelated persons for compensation.
202.7.3. Brewery. An establishment where malt beverages are manufactured and/or sold commercially and/or to be consumed on the premises.
202.7.6. Brewpub. Any eating establishment in which beer or malt beverages are manufactured or brewed, subject to the barrel production limitation prescribed in Code Section 3-5-36 for retail consumption on the premises and solely in draft form. As used in this paragraph, the term "eating establishment" means an establishment which is licensed to sell distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, or wines and which derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food; provided, however, that barrels of beer sold to licensed wholesale dealers for distribution to retailers and retail consumption dealers, as authorized pursuant to subparagraph (C) of paragraph (2) of Code Section 3-5-36, shall not be used when determining the total annual gross food and beverage sales.
202.8. Buffer. That portion of a lot established for open space purposes and intended to separate properties with different and possibly incompatible types of use. A buffer shall not be occupied with structures and facilities except as permitted by this ordinance. Where required by this ordinance, a buffer must include the installation of a suitable visual screen.
202.9. Building. Any structure having a roof and intended for shelter, housing or enclosure of persons, animals or property of any kind.
202.10. Building Height. The vertical distance of a building measured from the average elevation of the finished grade at the front of the building to the highest point of the building.
202.11. Building Line. That line which represents the distance a building must be set back from a zoning lot boundary line, measured at the foundation of the building.
202.12. Building, Principal. A building in which is conducted the principal use of the zoning lot on which said building is situated.
202.13. Care Home. A rest home, nursing home, convalescent home, home for the aged, or similar use established and operated on a profit or nonprofit basis to provide lodging and/or meals and/or domiciliary care for aged, infirmed, chronically ill or convalescent persons.
202.14. Centerline. That line surveyed and monumented by the proper governing authority as the centerline of the street or highway, or if such centerline has not been surveyed, it shall be that line running midway between the outside curbs or ditches of the street or highway, or the middle of the traveled roadway of the street.
202.14.5. Cidery. A place where hard cider is made commercially. Hard cider means an alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of the juice of apples including, but not limited to flavored or carbonated cider. For purposes of this ordinance, hard cider shall be deemed a malt beverage.
202.15. City Council. The mayor and council, being the governing authority of the City of Manchester, Georgia.
202.16. Clinic. An establishment where medical or dental patients are admitted for examination and treatment, but where there is no overnight lodging.
202.17. Club or Lodge. An incorporated or unincorporated association for civic, social, cultural, religious, fraternal, literary, political, recreation, or like activities, operated for the benefit of its members and not open to the general public.
202.18. Curb Cut. The point at which vehicular access is provided to a lot from an adjoining street.
202.19. Density. The number of dwelling units per acre of land used for residential purposes. Unless otherwise stated, density figures are to be in terms of total acres, or the land devoted to residential use inclusive of streets and other public lands.
202.20. Density, Disallowable. Disallowable density is more than 16 dwelling units per net acre.
202.21. Density, High. High density is eight to 16 dwelling units per net acre.
202.22. Density, Low. Low density is two dwelling units or fewer per net acre.
202.23. Density, Medium. Medium density is three to seven dwelling units per net acre.
202.23.5. Distillery. A place where whisky, bourbon, scotch or other distilled spirits are made and/or sold commercially and/or to be consumed on the premises. The term distilled spirits is defined as any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume.
202.24. Easement. The right or privilege of using another's property for purposes such as constructing and maintaining sanitary sewers, water mains, electric lines, telephone lines, storm sewers, gas lines, bicycle paths, or other purposes.
202.25. Elevation, Front. The view of a building or group of buildings as seen from directly in front of the structure.
202.25.5. Equestrian venue. A tract of land of 5 acres or more on which more than four adult horses, mules or burros are kept for the purpose of training, boarding, sales or breeding or where instruction pertaining to the same is given for a fee. For the purposes of this regulation this term also includes facilities for riding trails and rings, shows, competitive equestrian events and riding lessons.
202.26. Family Day Care Home. A private residence operated by any person who receives therein for pay for supervision and care fewer than 24 hours per day, without transfer of legal custody, three but not more than six children under 18 years of age who are not related to such person and whose parents or guardians are not residents in the same private residence.
202.27. Fallout Shelter. A structure or portion of a structure intended to provide protection to human life during periods of danger to human life from nuclear fallout, air raids, storms or other emergencies.
202.28. Farm. Any tract or parcel of land containing three or more acres which is devoted to the raising of agricultural products including, but not limited, to, soil crops, livestock, fish, fowl, and commercial timber, regardless of the quantity or value of production.
202.28.3. Farm Brewery. A brewery that is owned and operated by persons who are engaged in the production of a substantial portion of the agricultural produce used in its annual production.
202.28.6. Farm Winery. A winery that is owned and operated by persons who are engaged in the production of a substantial portion of the agricultural produce that is used in its wine production.
202.29. Feedlot. Any parcel of land, containing three or more acres, upon which the mechanical, hand or other feeding of livestock is routinely performed.
202.30. Flood Boundary. Those areas of the City of Manchester having a one percent chance or greater of being partially or completely inundated by floodwaters, either from a defined river, creek or stream, or from the unusual and rapid accumulation of runoff or surface water from any sources. For purposes of this ordinance, the 100-year floodplain shall be as shown on flood hazard boundary maps, published by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, or as determined from formal flood hazard studies prepared by the City of Manchester.
202.31. Floor Area. The area of a dwelling exclusive of attic, basement, garage, carport, patios, and open porches measured from the exterior face of the exterior walls of a dwelling. Also, the gross leasable floor area for any business or industry based on interior dimensions.
202.32. Garage. An accessory building or portion of a principal building used only for private storage of permitted motor vehicles.
202.33. Garage, Service. Any garage other than a private garage which is used for storage, repair, rental, servicing, washing, adjusting, or equipping of automobiles or other motor vehicles, but not including the storage or dismantling of wrecked or junked vehicles.
202.34. Garage, Repair. A garage intended to be used to make major automobile or other motor vehicle repairs; provided, that all body work and painting shall be conducted within fully enclosed buildings, and further provided there is no open storage of junked, wrecked vehicles, dismantled parts, or supplies visible beyond the premises.
202.35. Group Day Care Home or Center. A place operated by any person or group wherein are received for pay not less than seven nor more than 18 children under 18 years of age for care and supervision for less than 24 hours per day.
202.35.5. Growler Shop. A retail store selling a container that is filled by a licensee or employee of a licensee with beer or wine from a barrel, keg, or cask primarily for off premises consumption.
202.36. Guest House. Living quarters situated within an attached or detached accessory building located on the same premises as the principal building. Such quarters shall be used only by bona fide nonpaying guests or relatives of the owners or occupants of the principal building and shall not be rented or otherwise occupied as a separate dwelling.
202.36.5. Hobby Farming. A farm residence where a limited number of domestic animals are kept primarily for recreational purposes; buildings related to the hobby farm are clearly subordinate and incidental to the residential use; and the farming activity does not create or become a public nuisance, particularly in respect to smell, noise, traffic or parking.
202.37. Home Occupation. An occupation for financial gain or support conducted only by members of a family residing on the premises and entirely within the main dwelling.
202.38. Hotel. A building in which overnight accommodations without separate cooking facilities are provided to the public. The term "hotel" includes the terms "motel" and "tourist court."
202.39. Housing Terms.
A. Apartment Dwelling. One or more dwelling units, under a single ownership, located on one lot of land occupied by renters.
B. Cluster Dwelling. One of a series of attached and/or detached dwelling units developed under a single ownership.
C. Condominium Dwelling. An individually owned dwelling unit in an attached, detached, or multifamily structure, combined with joint ownership of common areas of the buildings and grounds.
D. Conventional Construction. A dwelling unit constructed on the building site from basic materials delivered to the site, and which is constructed in accordance with the statewide minimum building codes adopted by the State of Georgia.
E. DCA. Georgia Department of Community Affairs.
F. Dwelling. A building or portion thereof designed, arranged, or used principally for residential occupancy, not including manufactured homes, mobile homes, motels, hotels, boardinghouses, or rooming houses.
G. Dwelling Unit. One or more rooms within a building forming a separate, independent housekeeping establishment for use of one family involving owner or renter occupancy, with provisions for cooking, eating and sleeping, and which is physically set apart from other rooms or dwelling units in the same building.
H. Factory-Built Housing. An outdated term used to describe manufactured housing.
I. Garden Apartment Dwelling. A multifamily dwelling, one or two stories in height, with one dwelling unit per story, a private entrance for each dwelling unit, and where the area immediately surrounding the dwelling is landscaped and may contain recreation facilities for the private use of dwelling occupants.
J. HUD. U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
K. Manufactured Home. A factory-fabricated transportable structure of one or more sections at least eight feet in width and 40 feet in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet, manufactured in a model year not more than ten years before the date the current owner wishes to permit or locate said home under this ordinance, which is built on a permanent chassis designed to be used as a dwelling on a permanent foundation with wheels, axles, tongue and towing apparatus removed, when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein, and which complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards Act, bearing an insignia issued by HUD.
L. Manufactured Home Community. An area of land used or intended for use as a residential community occupied by manufactured homes with appropriate and adequate community services, recreation facilities, utilities, streets and sidewalks provided by the developer; where the resident owns or rents the manufactured home and rents the manufactured home space; but, where the homes are not on permanent foundations. Any area of land or place where two or more manufactured homes are parked for residential purposes, or where space is set aside and offered for rent for manufactured homes shall be considered a Manufactured Home Community for purposes of this ordinance.
M. Manufactured Home Space. An area of land within a manufactured home community designed to accommodate one manufactured home.
N. Manufactured Housing. A general term used to describe a type of housing which is produced, either completely or partially, in a factory, including manufactured homes, modular homes, and residential industrialized buildings. In the context of this ordinance, this term has no specific meaning.
O. Manufactured Housing Condominium. An area of land used or intended for use as residential land where homes are privately owned, arranged to occupy separate lots of land, where the residents own their individual dwelling unit and collectively own an undivided interest in common areas, and where homes are on permanent foundations.
P. Manufactured Housing Subdivision. An area of land used or intended for use as residential land, developed by selling individual lots either before or after dwelling unit is established on the lot; where the city provides services; where landowners follow local codes; and where homes are on permanent foundations.
Q. Modular Home. A factory-fabricated transportable dwelling unit built in one or more sections; constructed in accordance with the Standard Building Code (SBCCI) or a code establishing statewide minimum building standards adopted by the State of Georgia; showing proof of SBCCI, or other state certification; designed to be used as a dwelling on a permanent foundation, with wheels, axles, transporting lights, and tongue and/or towing apparatus removed; and which bears an insignia of the Southern Building Code Congress International (or state certifying agency).
R. Multifamily Dwelling. A building designed, constructed, altered or used for three or more adjoining dwelling units, with each dwelling unit having a party wall or walls and/or a party floor ceiling connecting it with at least one other dwelling unit located on one lot of land. A multifamily dwelling may be apartments or condominiums.
S. National Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards. The National Building Code for all manufactured homes built since June 15, 1976, written and administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (also known as the "HUD Code").
T. One-Family Attached Dwelling. A building containing two or more one-family attached dwelling units joined at one or more points by one or more party walls or other common facilities (not including the walls of an enclosed courtyard or similar area), and with property lines separating each dwelling unit, thus permitting zero-lot-lines.
U. One-Family Detached Dwelling. A single residential detached building designed for or containing one dwelling unit.
V. Patio Dwelling. A one-family dwelling in which all or a portion of the area required for side and rear yards may be consolidated into one or more garden court spaces within the walls of the dwelling unit.
W. Residential Apartment Dwelling. A dwelling unit located on the same lot as a one-family detached dwelling unit, usually in the form of a garage apartment or basement apartment.
X. Residential Industrialized Building (RIB). Any structure or component thereof which is wholly or in substantial part made, fabricated, formed, or assembled in manufacturing facilities for installation or assembly and installation on a building site and has been manufactured in such a manner that all parts or processes cannot be inspected at the installation site without disassembly, damage to, or destruction thereof; which bears an insignia of approval issued by the commissioner of the Georgia Department of Community Affairs; and which is used or intended to be used as a dwelling unit.
Y. Site-Built Home. See definition of "Conventional Construction."
Z. Stick-Built Home. See definition of "Conventional Construction."
AA. Townhouse Dwelling. One of a series of three or more attached dwelling units on separate lots which are separated from each other by fire walls extending at least from the lowest floor level to the roof.
BB. Travel Trailer. A vehicle designed as a temporary dwelling for travel or recreational uses, not more than eight feet in width and not more than 29 feet in length.
CC. Travel Trailer Park. A lot on which are parked two or more travel trailers for a period of less than 30 days.
DD. Two-Family Dwelling. A detached dwelling designed, constructed, altered or used for two adjoining dwelling units, with each dwelling unit having a party wall connecting it with the other dwelling unit, located on one lot (also known as a "duplex").
EE. Zero-Lot-Line Dwelling. An attached or detached one-family dwelling set against one or two lot lines rather than in the middle of the lot.
202.40. Institutional Use. A building, facility or land owned by a government, nonprofit corporation, association or entity, intended for public or semipublic use, such as courthouses, schools, churches, parks and recreation areas.
202.41. Junkyard. Any use on private property involving the parking, storage or disassembly of junked vehicles, or wrecked or nonoperable automobiles, trucks or other vehicles; storage, bailing or otherwise dealing in junk, animal hides, scrap iron and other metals, used paper, used cloth, used plumbing fixtures, old stoves, old refrigerators, and other old household appliances, and used brick, wood or other building materials. These uses shall be considered junkyards whether or not all or part of these operations are conducted inside a building or in conjunction with, in addition to or accessory to, other use of the premises.
202.42. Junked Vehicle. Any wrecked or nonoperable automobile, truck or other vehicle which does not bear a current license plate.
202.43. Kennel. The housing of four or more dogs, cats, or other domestic animals for the purpose of providing an income or revenue.
202.44. Land Area per Dwelling Unit. The amount of land in square feet required for each dwelling unit permitted on a zoning lot.
202.44.5. Live/Work Units. A one-family attached dwelling unit of at least two stories that contains a commercial component of not more than the lesser of 600 square feet in floor area or 40 percent of the dwelling's total floor area. Said commercial component shall be limited to the ground floor of the dwelling unit and shall be limited to the business and professional offices and retail uses permitted by zoning.
202.45. Loading Space. Space logically and conveniently located for pickup and delivery service, scaled to the vehicles expected to be used, and accessible to such vehicles at all times.
202.46. Lot. A parcel of land of varying size which is designated as a single unit of property. Unless otherwise stated in this ordinance, the word "lot" shall mean the same as "zoning lot" as herein defined.
202.47. Lot, Corner. A lot located at the intersection of two or more streets.
202.48. Lot, Double-Frontage. A lot, other than a corner lot, which has frontage on more than one street (also known as a "through lot").
202.49. Lot, Interior. A lot which has frontage on only one street or public way.
202.50. Lot, Zoning. A parcel of land in single ownership occupied or intended to be occupied by principal uses and accessory uses in accordance with the provisions of this ordinance. A zoning lot must have frontage on a street or public way and have at least the minimum land area required by this ordinance for the zoning district within which it is located. A lot of record may or may not be a zoning lot.
202.51. Lot Depth. The mean horizontal distance between the front and rear lot lines, measured in the general direction of the side lot lines.
202.52. Lot Width. The distance between side lot lines measured at the front building line. If a corner lot, the distance between lot lines measured along the front building line which parallels or more nearly parallels the rear lot line. (See definition of "Yard, Front.")
202.53. Lot of Record. An area designated as a separate and distinct parcel of land on a legally recorded subdivision plat or in a legally recorded deed.
202.53.2. Makers/Artisan Studio. A work studio, and/or retail space for artisans, craftsmen, and small-scale manufacturers to work in an individual or communal setting, where the activities produce little to no vibration, noise, fumes, or other nuisances more typical of industrial or manufacturing uses.
202.53.5. Meadery. A place where mead is made and sold commercially. Mead is defined as an alcoholic drink of fermented honey and water.
202.53.7. Microbrewery. The term used collectively to refer to breweries and brewpubs.
202.54. Nonconforming Use. Use of lands and/or structures for a purpose or in a manner contrary to provisions of this ordinance; generally of two types:
(1) Lawful where such use is rendered nonconforming by terms of this ordinance; and
(2) Unlawful where such use was illegal when commenced or became so thereafter prior to adoption of this ordinance.
202.55. Parking space. An area for off-street automobile parking.
202.56. Planning and Zoning Board (PZB). The City of Manchester, Georgia, Planning and Zoning Board.
202.57. Plat. A map, plan or layout of a county, city, town, section, or subdivision indicating the location and boundaries of properties.
202.57.5. Resort Vacation Cottages and Cabins. A residential style structure of at least 400 square feet with a kitchen and no more than four bedrooms that serves primarily as temporary lodging for visitors and is limited to short-term stays of less than 90 days.
202.58. Right-of-Way. A strip of land designated, reserved, dedicated, or purchased for the purpose of pedestrian or vehicular access, utility line installation, or other use.
202.59. Sign. Any name, identification, description, display, illustration or device that is affixed to, posted on or represented directly or indirectly upon a building, structure, land, vehicle or otherwise affixed for display in view of the general public and that directs attention to a product, place, activity, idea, person, institution or business.
202.60. Special Exception. A use which within certain districts specified by this ordinance is not permitted as a matter of right but may be permitted within these districts by the mayor and council after said council:
(1) Has reviewed the proposed plans for its use, its location, arrangement and design, its relationship to neighboring property and other conditions peculiar to the particular proposal which would determine its desirability or undesirability;
(2) Has found the proposal not to be contrary to the intent of this ordinance; and
(3) Has approved the use as specified.
202.61. Story. That portion of a building, not including a basement, between the surface of any floor and the surface of the floor next above it, or if there is no floor above, then, the space between the floor and the ceiling next above it.
202.62. Street. A public way for traffic which may or may not be publicly owned.
202.63. Street, Access. A street intended to carry traffic between commercial or similar uses and a thoroughfare.
202.64. Street, Private. A street that is privately owned and used in accordance with the wishes of the owner.
202.65. Street, Public. A street that is used for travel by the general public, whether or not it is owned by a public agency.
202.66. Structure. Anything constructed or erected which requires a fixed location on the ground or which is attached to something having a fixed location on the ground.
202.67. Subdivision. The division of a lot of record at time of enactment of this ordinance into two or more lots, building sites, or other divisions for the purpose, whether immediate or future, of sale, legacy, or building development, and includes all division of land involving a new street or a change in existing streets, and includes resubdivision, and where appropriate to the context, relates to the process of subdividing or to the land or area subdivided.
202.67.5. Tasting Room. An outlet for the promotion of a brewery, distillery, winery, meadery, or cidery providing samples of such beer, distilled spirits, wine, mead, or hard cider for consumption on premises and for the sale of such beverages at retail in closed packages for consumption off-premises.
202.68. Thoroughfare, Arterial. Highways, expressways, etc., which serve corridor movements and have trip length and travel density characteristics indicative of substantial statewide travel. Arterials link cities, large towns, and other major activity centers to form a network providing interstate and intercounty service. These routes are designed for relatively high speeds with minimum interference to through traffic. Access to arterials should be well controlled and limited to collector roads. While the primary function of an arterial road is traffic movement, some access to adjacent land can exist. Arterials can provide service to commercial and other employment centers. The intensity and design of any adjacent proposed development should be carefully evaluated to ensure that the intended function of the arterial as a safe, efficient thoroughfare is maintained.
202.69. Thoroughfare Classification. For purposes of this ordinance, the following classifications of thoroughfares shall apply:
A. Major Thoroughfares:
B. Collectors:
C. Local: All other city streets not classified as collectors or major thoroughfares.
202.70. Use, Conditional. That use which is permitted in a particular zoning district, but only under certain specified conditions.
202.71. Use, Principal. The main purpose for which a zoning lot is intended and for which it may be used.
202.72. Variance. A relaxation of the terms of this ordinance that will not be contrary to the public interest where, owing to conditions peculiar to the property, and not the result of the applicant, a literal enforcement of this ordinance would result in unnecessary and undue hardship. A variance cannot be granted to change the text of this ordinance, to reclassify property on the zoning map, or to allow a use not permissible within the district involved.
202.72.5. Winery. A commercial facility for the fermentation and processing of grapes or other produce into wine, or the refermentation of still wine into sparkling wine along with wine tasting rooms and accessory uses which must be largely incidental and subordinate to the primary winery use. The term includes various temporary, cultural and social events (catered banquets, receptions, concerts, food and wine festivals, races, etc.) that would not compromise the primarily agricultural appearance of the property. The term includes up to six overnight room accommodations for use by winery customers and business associates.
202.73. Yard. A required open space on a zoning lot that is left unoccupied with structures and facilities except as permitted in this ordinance. A yard may also be known as a setback.
202.74. Yard, Front. The area between the front property line and the front building line.
202.75. Yard, Rear. The area between the rear property line and the rear building line.
202.76. Yard, Side. The area between the side property line and the side building line.
202.77. Zoning Administrator. The person who has been designated by the mayor and council to administer the enforcement of this ordinance. In the absence of such designation, the City Manager or his or her designee of the City of Manchester, Georgia, shall perform the duties of the zoning administrator.
202.78. Zoning District. One or more geographic subdivisions of the City of Manchester, Georgia, as delineated and designated on the official zoning map within which the zoning regulations are uniform.
202.79. Zoning Map. The official map or maps of the City of Manchester, Georgia, indicating the location of zoning districts in the City of Manchester, Georgia.

1075:
The office of zoning administrator of the City of Manchester, Georgia, is hereby established.
302.1. Appointment. The zoning administrator shall be appointed by the mayor and council. The city manager of the City of Manchester, Georgia, is designated as the zoning administrator until such time as those duties are made the responsibility of another person.
302.2. Functions. The functions of the zoning administrator shall be as follows:
A. Have the primary responsibility for administering this ordinance, as well as other duties as determined by the mayor and council.
B. Keeps up-to-date on current laws, recent court decisions, and emerging techniques related to planning, zoning and development.
C. Assists the PZB in coordinating the review of all proposed development projects in the City of Manchester.
D. Provides information to the public on zoning and related matters.
E. Makes recommendations to the PZB and to the mayor and council on amendments to existing development regulations and on any new development regulations.
F. Maintains the official zoning map in a current manner, including all amendments to the map, in city hall.
G. Maintains the official copy of the zoning ordinance in city hall for public access.
H. Keeps copies of the zoning ordinance for sale to the public and zoning map for access by the public.
I. Takes application for rezonings and other amendments to the zoning ordinance and forwards the application, along with written comments concerning the proposed rezoning (or other amendment to the zoning ordinance) as examined under the criteria set forth in section 407, in light of other plans, studies, and regulations established by the City of Manchester, to the chairperson of the PZB within five days of the application for rezoning or other amendment.
J. Takes application for: appeals of decisions of zoning administrator and building official; variances, and special exceptions, and, forwards the application, along with written comments concerning the application as examined under the criteria set forth in sections 409, 410 and 411 to the city clerk within five days of the application.
K. Takes applications for development approval; and, forwards the application to the city engineer, in accordance with the development regulations of the City of Manchester.
L. Participates with review staff in reviewing applications for development under the development regulations.
M. Inspects or supervises the inspection of all projects during construction to ensure compliance with plans submitted with the application for building or other permit.
N. Maintains permanent records of amendments to the official zoning ordinance, including those sections as they appeared before the amendment and as they appear after the amendment.
O. Maintains permanent records of amendments to the official zoning map, including those districts as they appeared before the amendment and as they appear after the amendment.
P. Maintains permanent records of public hearings on zoning or other planning and development matters, including date, time and place of hearing; names of those in attendance, minutes of the hearings; and, any other pertinent information.
Q. Performs such other functions as prescribed by the mayor and council.
(Ord. of 1-9-2015)

The planning and zoning board of the City of Manchester, Georgia, is hereby established.
303.1. Members. The planning and zoning board (PZB) is composed of seven members appointed by the mayor and council. No member of the mayor and council may also serve as a member of the PZB. The members will each be a resident of the City of Manchester.
303.2. Terms. Each member of the PZB will serve for three years. Appointments will be made in January of each year when an appointment is due.
303.3. Officers. At the first meeting of the PZB each calendar year, the members will elect a chairperson and vice-chairperson. The chairperson will preside over all regular and special meetings of the PZB and may vote on matters. The vice-chairperson shall serve in the absence of the chairperson. The zoning administrator shall serve as secretary to the PZB. The secretary will keep minutes, studies, recommendations, and other documentation of PZB activities on file in city hall for access by the public.
303.4. Meetings.
a. The PZB shall adopt a regular meeting schedule in accordance with requirements of the Georgia Open Meetings Law and shall post at city hall the date, time and location of its regular meetings. The chairperson or any three members may call a special meeting at any time in accordance with applicable law. All meetings of the PZB shall be conducted in accordance with the Georgia Open Meetings Laws.
b. Meetings of the PZB will be for discussion and evaluation of zoning matters on which the PZB will make recommendations to the city council and will not constitute formal public hearings. Under procedural rules as may, from time to time, be adopted by the PZB, citizens of Manchester and persons having an interest in matters before the PZB are encouraged to attend and participate in the meetings. The PZB may, at its election, conduct a public hearing on proposed amendments to this ordinance, or in formulating planning policies; provided all public notice and hearings shall be given and conducted in accordance with section 408 of this ordinance.
303.5. Quorum. Four members of the PZB will constitute a quorum.
303.6. Functions. The functions of the PZB shall be as follows:
A. Conduct an unofficial public hearing for amendments to this ordinance in accordance with section 408
B. Conduct or authorize general and special studies, plans, or other projects related to: land use, zoning, economics, housing, marketing, population, transportation, community facilities and any other topic relative to planning and development.
C. Make recommendations to the mayor and council on rezoning applications within 45 days after receipt of the application by the zoning administrator; provided, however, no action by the PZB shall constitute "final action" on zoning decisions.

E. Make recommendations, where appropriate, to the mayor and council on special exceptions, variances, and conditional uses of land involved in a development request.
F. In carrying out its functions under this section, the PZB may, upon prior approval of the mayor and council, retain the services of professional land planners and consultants.
G. Other administrative functions as prescribed by the mayor and council relative to planning and development.

1077:
The functions of the mayor and council, as they relate to this ordinance, shall be as follows:
304.1. Conduct an official public hearing for amendments to this ordinance in accordance with section 408.
304.2. Approve or deny any proposed amendment to this ordinance, including any and all amendments to the official zoning map ; after first receiving comments and recommendations from the zoning administrator and the planning and zoning board.

The functions of the city engineer (either city employee or consultant) as they relate to this ordinance, shall be as follows:

The functions of the soil conservation district, as they relate to this ordinance, shall be as follows:
308.1. Provide written comments, upon request, on building plans, site plans, subdivision plans, locations of flood hazard area, soil erosion and sedimentation control plans, drainage plans, or any other subject, to the mayor and council, zoning administrator, or building official.

1082:
The functions of the regional development center, as they relate to this ordinance, shall be as follows:

Provide written comments, upon request, on building plans, site plans, subdivision plans, location of flood hazard area, rezoning of land (amendment to the official zoning map); other amendments to this ordinance or any other development regulation, plan, or study of the City of Manchester, or any other subject, to the mayor and council, zoning administrator, or building official.

1083:
The functions of an applicant, including applications for rezoning of land (amendment to the official zoning map) or other amendment to this ordinance; variance; special exception; and appeal of decisions of the zoning administrator, as they relate to this ordinance, shall be as follows:

1084:

1088:
Every building or structure erected or established in the City of Manchester shall be located on a zoning lot. In all cases, the principal building on a zoning lot shall be located within the buildable area formed by the building lines. In no case shall such buildings infringe beyond the building lines into the respective front, side or rear yards required for the district in which the zoning lot is located. Lanes associated with a drive-through window shall be considered part of the principal building when determining building location. In all residential zoning districts, there shall be no more than one principal building per lot.
(Ord. of 1-9-2015)
1089:
In interpreting and applying these regulations, the requirements contained herein are declared to be the minimum requirement necessary to carry out the purpose of these regulations. Except as hereinafter provided, these regulations shall not be deemed to interfere with, abrogate, annul or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever any easements, covenants, or other agreements between parties.
(Ord. of 1-9-2015)
1090:
