Certain terms and words are defined for the purpose of this chapter. Words used in the present tense shall include the future. The word "shall" is mandatory, and the word "may" is permissive.
a. As-built plans. Detailed construction plans showing completed improvements as constructed.
b. Boulevard. A street developed with two one-way pavements separated by a landscaped median.
c. City. The City of Manchester, Georgia.
d. Cluster residential development project. A residential development that provides for the grouping attached and detached residential dwellings on lots that may be smaller than allowed in a zoning district, for the purpose of preserving open space and natural terrain features, and economy in providing public facilities and services. On certain cluster home residential developments, fire-resistant materials may be required.
[e. Reserved.]
f. Commercial/office subdivision. A subdivision developed with streets and other improvements intended to serve lots for commercial and office development.
g. Comprehensive plan. The Manchester Comprehensive Plan adopted pursuant to the Georgia Planning Act of 1989, indicates the location and extent of future land uses, public facilities, transportation, and the city's long range development policies.
h. County. Meriwether County, Georgia or Talbot County, Georgia.
i. Covenant. An agreement or restriction placed on lots by a developer governing future land use or development which binds future purchasers of the lots.
j. Cul-de-sac. A dead-end local street opened at one end and closed at the other by a permanent, circular turnaround.
k. Crosswalk. A right-of-way within a block dedicated to public use, intended primarily for pedestrian use designed to provide access to adjacent roads and lots.
l. Dead-end street. A local street open at one end and closed at the other. Dead-end streets may have a cul-de-sac at the closed end, a "T" or "Y" turnaround, or dead-end for future extension to adjacent properties.
m. Dedication plat. A plat required for the dedication to the city of rights-of-way for streets, public easements for utilities, and other public improvements drawn in accordance with the Georgia Plat Act and suitable for recording.
n. Development permit. A permit issued by the city manager for construction of subdivision improvements and other development, including soil erosion and sedimentation control, rough clearing and grading, street and drainage construction, and storm water management.
o. Easement. A right granted by a property owner to the general public, a public utility, the city, or a private individual or corporation for the use of a portion of the owner's land for a specific purpose, or use as a means of access to other property. Easements shall be designated "public" or "private" depending upon the nature of the usage.
p. Engineer. A licensed professional engineer in the State of Georgia and registered through the State Board of Professional Engineers who is competent in the field of civil design.
q. Flood hazard area. The area threatened by periodic flooding as determined by data and maps provided by the Federal Emergency Management Administration, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, U.S. Soil Conservation Service, U.S. Army Corps Engineers, or hydrological studies utilizing generally accepted engineering practices. Flood hazard areas shall include all land underneath a permanent body of water, e.g., a lake, pond, river, and stream, and all land within the limits of a flood having a 100-year return frequency or better. Regulations for flood hazard areas are contained in the Manchester Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance.
r. County health department. The department responsible for enforcement of county health regulations including the issuance of permits for on-site sewage disposal systems and wells.
s. Improvements. Physical changes to the land which are necessary to create useable lots including (but not limited to) grading and paving streets, sewer and water facilities, hydrants, sidewalks, monuments, changes to existing utilities, and stormwater drainage and detention systems.
t. Improvements, construction plans. Detailed construction plans prepared by a professional engineer or landscape architect registered in the State of Georgia, for streets, including typical cross sections and grade profiles and elevations, layout and elevations of water and sanitary sewer facilities, along with drainage and stormwater management facilities, and soil erosion control.
u. Industrial subdivision. A subdivision developed with streets and other improvements intended to serve lots for industrial development, also known as planned industrial district or industrial park.
v. Landscape architect. A licensed professional landscape architect in the State of Georgia who is competent in the field of civil design.
w. Lot, building. A lot of record, or any combination of lots of record, held in single ownership, or in common ownership by more than one, which meets minimum lot area requirements established by the zoning district in which a given tract of land is located.
x. Lot, corner. A lot having frontage on two or more public streets at their intersection.
y. Lot divisions. The division of a tract or parcel of land into two or more lots. Lot must have minimum frontage on a city or county road, and comply with the Manchester Zoning Ordinance.
z. Lot of record. A lot which is drawn on an approved subdivision plat recorded in the office of the Meriwether or Talbot County Clerk of Superior Court, or a parcel described by metes and bounds, the description of which has been so recorded.
aa. Lot width. The distance between side lot lines, measured along the front yard building setback line as established by the Manchester Zoning Ordinance.
bb. Marginal access street. A local residential street paralleling and adjacent to a major arterial which provides access to abutting properties and protection from through traffic.
cc. City manager. The chief administrator for the city. The city manager is appointed by the mayor and council. Functions assigned to the city manager under this ordinance may be delegated by him, in writing, with approval of the mayor and council, to another employee of the city working under supervision of the city manager.
dd. Mayor and council. The elected governing body for the city. Referred to as "city council" in this chapter.
ee. Building and code enforcement department. The department responsible for administration and enforcement of the building codes and related construction codes, business licenses and issuance of development permits, soil erosion and sedimentation control, and construction inspections under direction of the city manager. This department is also responsible for administration of the comprehensive development plan, the zoning ordinance, development ordinance, stormwater management ordinance, landscape ordinance, and long-range development planning, under the direction of the city manager.
ff. Manchester Planning and Zoning Board. A board comprised of citizens appointed by the mayor and council to review and make recommendations on zoning, subdivision, and long range development plans. Referred to as the "PZB" in this ordinance.
gg. Manchester Public Works Department. The department responsible for design review construction inspection, and maintenance of streets, of water and sewer facilities within the city.
hh. Manchester Utilities Department. The department responsible for design review and construction inspection and operation of utilities and related facilities approved by the city.
ii. Pavement width. The cross section width of a paved road measured from edges of pavement.
jj. Perennial stream. Any stream which flows throughout the entire year, sometimes shown as a solid blue line on a United States Geological Survey (USGS) 7-minute Topographic Series Maps (1:24,000).
kk. Planned Unit Development (PUD). Development intended to encourage both residential and nonresidential land uses according to a master development plan, with related covenants and restrictions. Developments with PUD project may have flexibility in the application of development standards when approved according to a master development plan, and to promote the conservation of natural resources, and more efficient use of land.
ll. Plan. A developer's plan for the subdivision and development of land submitted to the city for approval under the ordinance, consisting of a minimum of:
1. Preliminary plat. A plan showing the basic design and layout of the subdivision.
2. Construction improvement plans in conformance with this chapter for all public improvements.
3. Final plat. A plat of a development with legal description of all lots, easements, and rights-of-way sufficient to reproduce the plat in the field, and which meets the requirements of the Georgia Plat Act. The final plat is intended for legal recording of lots, rights-of-way, easements, and restrictive covenants.
mm. Public open space. Land dedicated or reserved for use by the general public. It includes parks, recreation facilities, school sites, community or public building sites and similar spaces for public use.
nn. Public utility. Firms, corporations, or local government authorities providing gas, electricity, telecommunications service, and similar essential services.
oo. Road, city. Any road-paved or unpaved which is maintained by the city.
pp. Road, county. Any road-paved or unpaved which is maintained by Meriwether or Talbot County.
qq. Road, private. A road that is not maintained by the city or Meriwether or Talbot County. Private roads are under the ownership of private entities and maintained by individual property owners.
rr. Sewer, lateral. Sanitary sewer collection lines within a subdivision or development that transports effluent to larger trunk sewers for sewage treatment.
ss. Sewer, trunk. Main sanitary sewer lines which collect sewage from lateral sewer lines for transportation either directly to sewage treatment plants or to larger interceptor sewers entering a treatment plant.
tt. Sight distance; intersection sight distance. Sight distance for intersections with minor/major arterial roads use intersection sight distance measured from a driver's eye height of 3.5 feet to an object height of 4.25 feet.
uu. Sight distance; stopping distance relative to street design. The unobstructed vision on a horizontal plane along a street centerline from a driver-eye height of 3.5 feet and an object height of six inches.
vv. Soil erosion and sedimentation control plan. A plan for temporary and permanent facilities to control soil erosion and sedimentation from subdivision construction sites and commercial and industrial development sites, as required by the Manchester Soil Erosion and Sedimentation Control Ordinance, and the rules and regulations of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources Environmental Protection Division.
ww. Streets. A street includes the land between the right-of-way lines, whether improved or unimproved, and may be comprised of pavement, shoulders, curb and gutter, sidewalks, drainage ditches and structures within the street right-of-way lines. Streets are classified as follows:
1. Expressway. The expressway system includes high volume limited access thoroughfares through the county and region beyond.
2. Major arterial. An arterial street which is designed or intended for moderate to high levels of traffic flow within the city and county and region beyond and also includes the state and national highway system in the city and county.
3. Minor arterial. An arterial street similar in function of a major arterial but which is intended to provide moderate levels of traffic flow and greater access to abutting properties. Minor arterials serve as traffic feeder to major arterials and for cross-county and regional traffic.
4. Collector street. A street which carries traffic from local streets to minor and major arterial streets, and may include the principal entrance of a development.
5. Local street. A street designed to provide access to adjoining properties within a subdivision or other development.
6. Stub street. A dead-end street at adjoining property lines intended for future extension to serve the development of adjoining areas.
7. Mountain Springs Village Street. A Village Street is intended for moderate levels of traffic flow within mixed-use areas of the Mountain Springs zoning district.
8. Mountain Springs Rural Residential Street. A rural residential street is intended to provide access to residential properties while maintaining a rural aesthetic. A rural residential street provides for low levels of traffic flow.
9. Mountain Springs Split Street. A split street consists of two adjacent, one-way streets with green space between the two streets. A split street is intended to maintain a rural, forested aesthetic. A split street provides for low levels of traffic flow.
xx. Stub-out service. Sanitary sewer connection facilities within the street right-of-way provided from lateral sewer line to the private property line for connection to building sewer lines.
yy. Subdivision. The division of a parcel or tract of land for the purpose of creating sites for development, the rearrangement of existing lot lines, or transfer of ownership.
zz. Subdivision re-plat. A plat submitted for changes in the arrangement of existing lots, rights-of-way or improvements in an existing approved and recorded subdivision.
aaa. Surveyor. A registered land surveyor in the State of Georgia registered by the state board of licensing.
bbb. Townhouse residential development project. A residential development project (as part of a PUD) that includes attached residential dwellings sharing common walls with fire rating according to the life safety code, and which are planned for individual ownership of the dwelling units and land thereafter.
ccc. Utilities. Gas, electrical, and telecommunications facilities installed by a public utility company, or local government authorities.
ddd. Wetlands. Areas defined as wetlands by federal law and regulations.
eee. Zoning ordinance. The official zoning ordinance and zoning map as adopted by the mayor and council.

1180: Within the territorial limits of this city, no person shall subdivide or rearrange a lot line of any lot or parcel of land, grade and install streets and utilities, or make other improvements to the land without complying with the provisions of this chapter. The Meriwether or Talbot County Clerk of Superior Court shall record no final subdivision plat unless the same has been approved as provided herein. No building permits shall be issued and no public improvements or services shall be authorized or installed in any unapproved subdivision. The review and approval process of a subdivision shall include a pre-application conference and preliminary plan, construction improvements plans, soil erosion and sedimentation control plan, and a final plat. "As-built" construction plans for public improvements are required to be submitted with the subdivider's final plat.
1181:
A. Purpose of conference. The subdivider shall consult with the city manager for advice and assistance prior to preparation of the preliminary plat and application for approval. This will enable the subdivider to become familiar with the approval process, required documents, inspections, the comprehensive plan, subdivisions improvement standards adopted by the city council, and development factors which may impact the immediate area near the subdivision. For subdivisions that require access onto a state highway, the subdivider is required to consult with the district engineer for the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT). The subdivider shall consult with the public works director for access onto city streets, and for improvements to existing streets.
B. Presentation of preliminary plan review. The subdivider shall be prepared to present a preliminary plan at or following the pre-application conference. The preliminary concept plan shall be a general design of the proposed subdivision including boundaries of the proposed subdivision, topographic contours, layout of lots and streets, size and dimensions of the property and proposed lots [including lot area], open space and other planned improvements.
C. [Review and transmit; written response.] Following the pre-application conference the city manager in consultation with the planning and zoning board (PZB) shall review the preliminary plan and transmit the subdivider within 15 working days a written response, providing the following information:
1. Conformance to standards in the zoning ordinance.
2. Conformance of the proposed subdivision to the comprehensive plan and any other plans and development policies of the city.
3. Any recommendations or reports from the city engineer or other city departments.
4. Any additional information relative to the subdivision approval process or development standards.
5. Recommendations to improve the development and design of the subdivision.
1182:
A. The city manager in consultation with the PZB shall determine that the proposed subdivision meets the requirements of the Manchester Zoning Ordinance and the property is in the correct zoning district. Following written notification by the city manager that the proposed preliminary plan complies with the zoning ordinance and the requirements of this chapter, and recommendations for improving the development, the subdivider may proceed with preparing a construction improvement plan as provided in this chapter.
B. If the property is not in the correct zoning district for the proposed subdivision development, the subdivider shall submit an application for rezoning according to the procedures of the Manchester Zoning Ordinance. The preliminary plan for the proposed subdivision shall be submitted with the rezoning application for review and recommendation by the PZB, and action by the city council.
1183:
A. The subdivider shall file with the city manager seven copies of the construction improvement plan. A plan review fee of $500.00 shall be paid by the subdivider at the time of submission. The construction improvements plan shall be reviewed by various city departments, including the public works department, the water and sewer department, building and code enforcement department; police department, fire department; and any other city and county organizations that will be impacted by the subdivision. The city manager shall notify the school district about the proposed subdivision. The plan review process shall determine compliance with the regulations of this ordinance and the zoning ordinance and make any changes necessary to improve the subdivision.
1. If the plans are determined to be incomplete or otherwise deficient by the city, they shall be returned to the subdivider for changes and corrections.
2. If the plans are approved with modifications, the changes shall be indicated on the plat. A copy of the plans with changes indicated shall be returned to the subdivider who shall have the revisions made by the engineer who prepared the plans.
3. Once the preliminary plan has been reviewed and required revisions, if any, are made, the preliminary plat shall be submitted to the PZB and subsequently to the city council for final approval.
4. Following review and approval of the preliminary plat by the PZB and approval by the city council, the subdivider shall proceed with construction improvements plans.
1184:
A. The plat shall have the following information:
1. Description:
a. Proposed name of subdivision, including unit, phase, and lines separating phases and/or units.
b. Names, addresses, and telephone numbers of subdivider, engineer, landscape architect, and surveyor. Show 24-hour contact person.
c. Graphic scale, north arrow, and date: the north point shall be identified as magnetic, true, or grid north.
d. Location map showing the relationship of the subdivision site to the surrounding area, including directions and distances to readily identifiable landmarks in the surrounding area.
e. Acreage to be subdivided.
f. Number of lots.
g. Density in dwellings per acre [gross].
h. Total lineal feet of roads [per phase and total].
i. Zoning district of the property, including all setback provisions, as well as any special conditions of zoning imposed by the city (i.e., lots sizes, number of lots, minimum house size).
2. Existing conditions:
a. Topographic contours and vertical intervals of not more than two feet when a new street is involved in a subdivision including outline of wooded areas, vegetation, and surface drainage.
b. Topographic data shall be based on field survey or aerial survey.
c. Deed record names and addresses of adjoining property owners or subdivision, along with zoning of the adjacent parcels.
d. In case of a re-subdivision, a copy of existing plat with proposed resubdivision imposed thereon.
e. Show whether or not any portion of the project is in a 100-year flood plain or contains known statutory wetlands.
f. Location of existing and platted property lines, location, width, and names of all platted roads, railroads, utility rights-of-way, public areas, existing buildings or structures.
g. Existing sewers, water mains, drains, culverts or other underground facilities within the tract or within the right-of-way of boundary roads with sizes, grades, and invert elevations from field surveys or other sources. All sizes and data on all utilities shall be provided.
h. Location of streams, lakes, wetlands, and land subject to a 100-year flood hazard, including contour elevations. State if elevations are taken from a surveyed stream on a FEMA map or if the elevations are from an independent study (HEX-2, QUICK-2, etc.). Wetland areas shall be field located.
i. Notation that live streams and/or wetlands lie/do not lie within this subdivision, or unit, or phase. Provide a copy of wetlands delineation report from a registered soil scientist in the State of Georgia.
j. Existing drainage patterns. The boundaries of the pre-developed drainage basins shall be shown on a map. The map shall include the number of acres in each basin, the pre-developed runoff coefficient, and the time of concentration.
3. Proposed conditions:
a. Layout and names of proposed roads, alleys, public walkways/bikeways (i.e., sidewalks, trails, paths, bicycle facilities), with width of pavement and rights-of-way.
b. Lot dimensions, including lot area. Lots with detention ponds must meet minimum zoning area requirements outside the area of the detention pond. Show all existing and proposed easements. Show drainage easements for storm drainage pipes which cross individual lots.
c. Flood elevations on any lots within a 100-year flood hazard area. In addition, the foundation footing elevation that is a minimum of one foot above the established 100-year flood elevation shall be shown. This data may be shown either on the lot layout or in tabular form.
d. Construction plans of streets including typical cross section and grade profiles. Show percent of each grade and length of each vertical curve. The minimum centerline stopping sight distance for interior streets is 200 feet.
e. Show the centerline stopping distance for all points of access onto county roads. Show posted speed limit of existing roads.
f. Construction plans of storm drainage systems with pipe sizes, length, grade, location of outlets, runoff and velocity calculations, etc. All storm drainage systems carrying off-site runoff shall be designed for the 100-years storm event. All storm pipes within the county right-of-way shall be asphalt coated corrugated metal pipe.
g. Improvements construction plan of water supply system with pipe sizes and location of hydrants, valves, and all appurtenances.
h. Improvement construction plan of sanitary sewers with grades, service, pipe size, and points of discharge and connection to other trunk or lateral sewers.
i. Easements for drainage and future sanitary sewers along all side and rear lot lines.
j. Proposed soil erosion and sedimentation control.
k. Final contours. In some cases, the street profiles will suffice in showing the amount of cut and fill; however, in many cases, final contours need to be shown on the plans.
l. Stormwater management. A hydrological study should be included and the necessary outlet control structures should be shown on the plan. No increase in runoff or velocity will be permitted. Attach engineer's certification that the improvements will not adversely impact downstream properties.
m. Proposed drainage patterns. The boundaries of the post-developed drainage basins shall be shown on a map. The map shall include the number of acres in each basin, the post-developed runoff coefficient, and the time of concentration.
n. Show a five-foot high fence on all detention ponds with a 100-year ponding elevation over four feet.
o. Detail drawings. Any structural practice used should be explained and illustrated with detail drawings and must, at a minimum, meet city standards.
p. Show the following notes on all plans:
1) A 20-foot storm sewer and sanitary sewer easement exists along each property line and along each lot line, centered on lot lines, for future drainage lines.
2) All storm drains shall be extended a minimum of 30 feet behind any future residence or building.
3) Grade stakes shall be set on all streets prior to any street grading. An as-built subgrade centerline profile shall be submitted and approved by city prior to the installation of curb and gutter or waterlines.
4) An as-built detention pond detail and revised hydro study shall be submitted to the city prior to installation of the water line or curb and gutter.
5) All undisturbed buffers shall be field located; staked and flagged or marked with "tenzar" (or similar type fencing); and shall be submitted to the city for approval prior to grading.

When the final plat has been approved by the city manager, the subdivider shall supply one original drawing of the final plat on mylar or sepia in black ink, as well as ten copies (blue lines) of the final plat prepared by a licensed professional engineer or landscape architect and a surveyor, minimum size 8½ inch by 11 inch, maximum size 17 inch by 22 inch. 1188: Prior to the approval of the final plat by the city manager, the subdivider shall pay a fee of $50.00 per lot shown on the final plat to the City of Manchester.
1189:
A. The final plat shall be prepared by a registered professional engineer or landscape architect and a surveyor, at a scale of 100 feet or less to the inch and shall provide the following information:
1. Name of the subdivision, including unit and/or phase of development (if applicable).
2. North point, scale, and date.
3. Names and addresses of the owners of record of the property to be subdivided.
4. Subdivider name, address, and phone number(s).
5. Name, addresses, phone number(s), and registration seal of the engineer or landscape architect and a surveyor who prepared the final plat.
6. Certification by surveyor that all monuments exist and their sizes, locations, and materials are correctly shown on the plat.
7. Legal description of the property including reference to land lot and district lines; street right-of-way lines; easements and other rights-of-way; property lines of lots and other sites with accurate dimensions to nearest 0.01 of a foot; bearings and angles on all lines; radii, arcs, and central angles of all curves with readings to the nearest minute.
8. Blocks designated by letter and lots by numerical order.
9. Current zoning, including setbacks and any special conditions placed on the rezoning of the property, or, stipulated in deed restrictions or restrictive covenants (i.e., minimum house size, type of construction).
10. The layout of the subdivision, including the following information:
a. All street right-of-way boundaries, street names, addresses, tax identification numbers, bearings, angles of intersection, and right-of-way and easement widths.
b. The lengths of all arcs, including radii, points of curvature, tangent bearings, and the length and bearing of the long cord of every arc.
c. Drainage, sanitary sewer, and utility easements along all side and rear lot lines and natural or artificial watercourses as required in chapter 4 [of this appendix].
d. Detention pond maintenance and access easement to be shown, minimum 20 feet to a public right-of-way.
e. Location of all storm drains including pipe sizes.
f. Any buffer areas required in the zoning ordinance, including statements whether or not the buffer areas are to be landscaped, undisturbed, fenced, or a combination-type buffer.
g. All lot lines measured to 0.01 of a foot. The bearings shall be indicated for all lot lines to the nearest second. The error of closure should not be less than one foot in 10,000.00 feet.
h. Individual lot sizes measured in square feet. This figure may be placed on the lot or in a table with addresses and tax parcel identification numbers. All lots with detention ponds must meet the minimum zoning area requirements outside the area of the detention pond.
i. The outline of all property to be dedicated or reserved for public use, or to be reserved for common use of all property owners in the subdivision with the purpose of the dedication or reservation indicated. This shall include cemeteries or grave sites as stated in section 4.45.
j. Location of sidewalks and pedestrian and/or bicycle ways.
k. Location and elevation of any 100-year flood hazard area, including the foundation elevation which is one foot above the established 100-year flood elevation for each lot located within the flood hazard area. This flood hazard area shall include both studied and unstudied streams, including drainage ways as designated on the preliminary plat.
l. The following notations and certifications:
Notation that "Live streams and/or wetlands lie (do not lie) within this subdivision, or unit and phase." If wetlands do lie within this subdivision, or unit and phase, the plat must include the following notation: "Wetlands shown on this plat are under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Lot owners may be subject to penalty of law for disturbance to these wetland areas without proper authorization."
Notation that "The Lot owners may be subject to penalty of law for any unauthorized land distributing activity conducted on their property.
Notation that "All storm drains shall be extended a minimum of 30 feet behind any future residence or building, and shall empty or drain into a sufficient drainage easement or watercourse."

1190: Lot divisions are the dividing of individual tracts of land into two or more separate lots without creating a subdivision as defined herein(no new street or utilities required). All lot divisions shall conform to the requirements of the Manchester Zoning Ordinance. The city manager shall have the authority to approve lot division. No building permit shall be issued for a tract of land created as the result of a lot division without the approval of the city manager.
1191:
A plat shall be prepared by a registered engineer or landscape architect and surveyor, and shall provide the following information:
1. North arrow, scale, and date.
2. Names and addresses of the owners of record of the property to be subdivided.
3. Subdivider name and address.
4. Name, address, and registration seal of the surveyor who prepared the final plat.
5. Certification by a surveyor that all monuments exist and their size, locations, and materials are correctly shown on the plat.
6. Legal description of the property, including reference to land lot district lines; street right-of-way lines; easements and other rights-of-way; property lines of lots and other sites with accurate dimensions to nearest 0.01 of a foot; bearings and angles on all lines: radii, arcs, and central angles of all curves with readings to the nearest second.
7. Blocks designated by letter and lots by numerical order.
8. The layout of the lot division including the following information:
a. All street right-of-way boundaries, street names, addresses, tax parcel identification numbers, bearings, angles of intersection, and right-of-way easement widths.
b. The lengths of all arcs, including radii, points of curvature, tangent bearings, and the length and bearing of the long cord of every arc.
c. Drainage and utility easements along all side and rear lot lines and watercourses, as required in Chapter 4, Improvements Standards [of this appendix].
d. All lot lines measured to nearest 0.01 of a foot. The bearings shall be indicated for all lot liens to the nearest second. The error of closure should not be less than one foot in 10,000 feet.
e. Individual lot sizes measured in square feet. This figure may be placed on the lot or in a table with addresses and tax parcel identification numbers.
9. Current zoning, including the required setback lines by the zoning ordinance and any other setback lines established by public authority or stipulated in the deed restrictions.
10. Protective covenants or deed restrictions, if any, shall be placed directly on the final plat or attached in form for recording.
11. Soil survey prepared by a qualified, state-registered soil scientist and certified for approval by the health department.
12. Location and elevation of any 100-year flood hazard area, including the minimum foundation elevation for each lot affected by the 100-year flood hazard.
13. Statement on the existence of wetlands or live streams on the site.
1192: A plat is required for the dedication to the city of right-of-way and public improvements such as roads or sewer or water lines, and which will provide access or service to development, or which will serve future development in an area or sited for public facilities as described in chapter 5 [of this appendix]. The approval process for dedication plats shall be the same as for a final subdivision plat. A two-year maintenance bond or letter of credit shall be required for all public improvements as required for final plats.
1193:
The plat shall be prepared by a registered professional engineer or landscape architect and a surveyor at a scale of 100 feet or less to the inch and shall provide the following information:
1. An accurate legal description of the property to be dedicated, including reference land lot lines.
2. The names and addresses of the owners of record of the property, the subdivider, and the engineer or landscape architect and surveyor who prepared the plat. The registration seal of the engineer or landscape architect and surveyor shall be on the plat.
3. North arrow, scale, and date.
4. The locations, widths, and names of any platted streets and easements adjacent to the property.
5. The locations, sizes, and grades of any existing sewers, water mains, culverts, and other underground structures adjacent to the property.
6. Contour elevations at two-foot intervals.
7. The layout, names and right-of-way widths of all streets, easements, or tracts of land to be dedicated.
8. The location and sizes of all proposed catch basins, culverts, and other drainage structures.
9. All plat boundary lines measured to the nearest 0.01 of a foot, and bearings and angles based on an accurate field survey.
10. The location of all permanent reference monuments as specified in chapter 4 [of this appendix].
11. The layout of the proposed improvements, including the following information when applicable:
a. Street right-of-way boundaries, names, bearings, angles of intersections, and widths.
b. Easement boundaries, bearings, and widths for improvements to be dedicated.
12. The 100-year flood elevation taken from either a FEMA flood insurance map or from an individual study as directed by the building and code enforcement department.
1195:
The location, arrangement, extent, width, and grade of all streets shall conform to this ordinance, and shall be considered in relation to existing and planned streets, topographical conditions, public safety and convenience, and proposed use of land to be served by the streets. The layout of a subdivision shall conform to the requirements of the zoning ordinance and design principles described in this ordinance.
Cross reference— Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 66.
1196: Whenever a tract to be subdivided includes any part of a major arterial, or collector street, such part of said street shall be installed by the subdivider in the location and at the full width indicated by the functional classification for right-of-way and pavement widths indicated in this ordinance.
1197:
A. Where appropriate to the subdivision design, proposed streets shall be continuous and in alignment with existing, planned or platted streets with which they are to connect.
B. Proposed streets shall be extended to the boundary lines of the tract to be subdivided, unless prevented by topography or other physical conditions for the coordination of the layout of the subdivision with existing and future development of adjacent tracts.
C. When there exists adjoining the tract to be subdivided a dedicated or platted half-width street or alley, the other half-width shall be platted.
Cross reference— Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 66.
1198:
Whenever a proposed subdivision has streets that will enter on a state highway maintained and controlled by the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT), the preliminary plat shall be submitted by the developer to the GDOT district engineer for approval.
Cross reference— Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 66.
1199: When a tract fronts on a state highway, major arterial, or minor arterial street, the subdivider may be required to have all residential lots to be provided with frontage only upon a collector or local street.
1200:
A. The design of street access to subdivisions shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations relating to street and intersection design and shall be consistent with accepted engineering standards and practices.
B. The maximum number of lots per a single subdivision entrance is 35, unless due to the peculiar shape, or the topography of a tract of land or other unusual condition whereby a variance must be obtained from the city council. The total number of entrances required for a subdivision shall be determined by the city based on the number of lots within the subdivision. Within the Mountain Springs zoning district, the maximum number of lots for single-family homes shall be 250 lots per entrance from any pre-existing public right-of-way including state highways, county roads, and city roads.
C. At its discretion, the city council may require a multi-lane boulevard entrance to a proposed subdivision development consistent with the city's design requirements.
(Ord. of 07-16-2023(1), 7-16-2023)
Cross reference— Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 66.
1201:
Although certain conditions may require additional right-of-way, the minimum width of street right-of-way, measured from lot line to lot line, shall not be less than as follows:
1. Major arterial—100 feet.
2. Minor arterial—80 feet
3. Collector street—80 feet
4. Local street—60 feet with curbs
5. Cut-de-sac—55-foot radius turnaround, residential local streets with curbing.
6. "T" or "Y" turnaround same as required street right-of-way.
7. Mid-block pedestrian way—ten feet.
8. Mountain Springs Village Street — 60 feet
9. Mountain Springs Rural Residential Street - 30 feet
10. Mountain Springs Split Street - 80 feet
(Ord. of 07-16-2023(1), 7-16-2023)

B. Where it is determined to be practical to require the dedication of the additional half when adjoining property is subdivided, the other half of the street shall be platted to create a full width right-of-way serving the adjoining tracts of land.

1205: The posted speed limit on all local streets within a subdivision shall [be] 30 miles per hour. The Manchester Police Department shall determine the speed limit for all other street classifications, subject, as necessary, to approval by GDOT.
1206:
Curbs shall be required in all residential subdivisions, with the exception of the Mountain Springs zoning district which shall not be required to have curbs. Curbs shall be required for streets in commercial and industrial subdivisions. Curbs in all subdivisions shall be L-back curbs 24 inches wide, 6 inches high, with an 1 8-inch gutter. All curbs shall be constructed of Portland cement concrete. Curbs shall be designed to provide handicapped access at street intersections, wherever sidewalks are constructed.
(Ord. of 07-16-2023(1), 7-16-2023)
1207:
Grades on major and minor arterials shall not exceed five percent and grades on local residential streets shall not exceed 12 percent. The minimum grade on any street shall be one percent.
When required by existing topography, grades of up to 25% are allowed on Mountain Springs Village Streets, Mountain Springs Rural Residential Streets, and Mountain Springs Split Streets within the Mountain Springs zoning district.
(Ord. of 07-16-2023(1), 7-16-2023)
Cross reference— Streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 66.
1208: The radius of horizontal curves on local residential streets within a subdivision shall be no less than 150 feet. The horizontal radius for collector and arterial streets or any streets with a designed speed of more than 25 miles per hour shall comply with AASHTO standards.
1209: All changes in grade shall be connected by vertical curves that are as long as conditions permit and under no circumstances should they be shorter than established minimums prescribed by approved highway design methods.

1211:
A. Street intersections shall be as nearly as right angles as possible. In residential subdivisions no intersection shall be at an angle of less than 80 degrees nor more than 100 degrees.
B. Street intersection in commercial and industrial subdivisions shall be at an angle of not less than 90 degrees.
C. The minimum curb radius at street intersections shall not be less than 20 feet in residential subdivisions. A minimum 25-foot radius shall be required at intersections with existing collector and arterial streets maintained by the city or county.
D. The minimum curb radius of street intersections for industrial and commercial subdivisions shall be 50 feet.
E. Pedestrian ramps shall be designed for all intersections in accordance with standard drawings for subdivisions and residential developments designed to include sidewalks and shall meet the minimum standards in regards to the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). The curb shall be depressed to accommodate future installations at the same time as the street.
1212: Street intersections shall have a minimum centerline offset of at least 125 feet.
1213: A tangent of at least 100 feet long shall be introduced between reverse curves on major and minor arterial streets, or on any street where the posted speed limit will be 35 miles per hour or greater.
1214:
A. Local streets designed to have one end permanently closed and not connected with any existing street, proposed future street, or not intended to extend to the property line of an adjacent tract, shall be no longer than seven times the lot width provided by the zoning ordinance, unless necessary due to the topographic or other physical conditions of the property.
1. Permanent dead-end streets. Permanent dead-end streets shall be joined by a cul-de-sac with a paved turnaround having an outside diameter of 80 feet (40-foot radius) and a right-of-way of at least 110 feet diameter. Dead-end streets designed to be permanent and that exceed more than 800 feet in length may be required to have a cul-de-sac turn around midway between the entrance intersection and the end of the street to provide maneuvering for emergency vehicles, when the dead-end street is the only street in a subdivision.
2. Temporary dead-end streets. Stub streets that are intended to provide access for future development within a tract of land or adjacent tracts shall be required to have a temporary turnaround area having a diameter of at least 80 feet, consisting of six inches of graded aggregate base.
B. For subdivisions with a temporary turnaround, it shall be required of the subdivider to provide a bond or letter of credit equal to the cost of permanent cul-de-sac construction, for a period of two years. Failure of the subdivider to extend the street or to construct a permanent cul-de-sac shall result in the city using the bond or letter of credit funds to complete the cul-de-sac construction.
1215:
There shall be no private street platted in any subdivision. Every lot in subdivided property shall be served from and shall have frontage onto a street dedicated to the city; provided, however, when a developer intends to build a "gated community", upon approval of the mayor and council, after review by the city attorney, such private streets may be approved if protective covenants make reasonable provision for maintenance by a mandatory homeowners association.
Private streets, roads, or drives shall be permitted within the Mountain Springs zoning district when such thoroughfares are maintained by a homeowners' association. Private streets, roads, and drives in the Mountain Springs zoning district are allowed to be gravel, but all public streets must be paved. Private streets, roads, and drives in the Mountain Springs zoning district are allowed to be gated. In the Mountain Springs zoning district, private drives serving multiple lots are allowed, and gravel thoroughfares for private drives are acceptable.
(Ord. of 07-16-2023(1), 7-16-2023)
1216: Alleys may be provided at the rear of lots in residential, commercial, and industrial subdivisions when approved by the community development director.
1217:
A. Every subdivision developer shall be required to follow the requirements of the soil erosion and sedimentation control ordinance, to grade and improve streets, alleys and rights-of-way, to install curbs or ditches when required and to install street name signs in accordance with city specifications. Every subdivider shall be required to comply with the subdivision inspection procedures in chapter 6 [of this appendix].
B. All street design and construction and related material shall be in strict accordance with Georgia Department of Transportation "Standard Specifications, Construction of Roads and Bridges", 1993 Edition, and all revisions thereto and the requirements of sections 4-24 and 4-25. Where circumstances dictate variations from the standard specifications upon recommendation of the city engineer, the city council may vary the requirements, provided the design of materials accepted are in all ways commensurate with good practice.
C. All materials, equipment, labor and other matters related to street construction shall be provided by the developer. The following is a summary of the improvements required:
1. Grading. All streets, roads, and alleys shall be graded to their full width right-of-way by the subdivider so that the pavements and sidewalks, when installed in the future, can be constructed on the same level plane. The preparation of the right-of-way before grading is started and the construction of cuts and fills shall be accomplished according to the specifications of the city.
All stumps, tree limbs, and other organic material shall be removed from the rights-of-way and building site areas and disposed of in accordance with law in a permitted landfill. No stumps, limbs or other organic material, including building debris, scrap lumber, etc., shall be buried anywhere in the subdivision development. In developments over ten acres, the city manager may issue a permit authorizing burning, using approved pit burners; provided all other state and local regulatory permits are first obtained and the city is not under a burn warning or hazardous air conditions alert.
2. [Profile.] Three copies of an as-built subgrade centerline profile shall be submitted. The profile shall include both proposed and as-built centerline elevations at every even station. No curb and gutter or waterlines shall be installed prior to subgrade approval.
3. Storm damage. An adequate drainage system, including necessary curb, pipes, culverts, headwalls, intersectional drains, drop inlets, bridges, swale ditches, and detention areas, shall be provided for the proper drainage of all surface water and prepared by a registered professional engineer or landscape architect.
4. Roadway surfacing. After preparation of the subgrade the roadbed shall have base material and paving applied according to city specifications.
